title: द्विचत्वारिंशत्तमोऽध्यायः
titleEn: Adhyaya 42 · Duryodhana claims the Pandavas are discovered

summary.en: Duryodhana tells Bhishma, Drona and Kripa that the Pandavas have broken their pact by appearing before the thirteen years are complete, and that whoever this is, they must fight. He orders the cattle sent ahead and the army arrayed for battle.
summary.kn: ಹದಿಮೂರು ವರ್ಷ ಪೂರ್ಣವಾಗುವ ಮೊದಲೇ ಕಾಣಿಸಿಕೊಂಡು ಪಾಂಡವರು ಒಪ್ಪಂದ ಮುರಿದಿದ್ದಾರೆ, ಇವನು ಯಾರಾದರೂ ಹೋರಾಡಲೇಬೇಕು ಎಂದು ದುರ್ಯೋಧನನು ಭೀಷ್ಮ, ದ್ರೋಣ, ಕೃಪರಿಗೆ ಹೇಳುತ್ತಾನೆ. ಗೋವುಗಳನ್ನು ಮುಂದೆ ಕಳುಹಿಸಿ ಸೈನ್ಯವನ್ನು ವ್ಯೂಹದಲ್ಲಿ ನಿಲ್ಲಿಸಲು ಆಜ್ಞಾಪಿಸುತ್ತಾನೆ.
summary.hi: दुर्योधन भीष्म, द्रोण और कृप से कहता है कि तेरह वर्ष पूरे होने से पहले प्रकट होकर पाण्डवों ने प्रतिज्ञा तोड़ी है, और यह कोई भी हो, उन्हें लड़ना ही होगा। वह गौओं को आगे भेजने और सेना को व्यूह में खड़ा करने का आदेश देता है।
summary.te: పదమూడేళ్లు పూర్తి కాకముందే కనిపించి పాండవులు ఒప్పందాన్ని భంగపరిచారని, ఇతడు ఎవరైనా పోరాడవలసిందేనని దుర్యోధనుడు భీష్మ ద్రోణ కృపులకు చెబుతాడు. గోవులను ముందుకు పంపి సైన్యాన్ని వ్యూహంలో నిలపమని ఆజ్ఞాపిస్తాడు.
summary.ta: பதின்மூன்று ஆண்டுகள் நிறைவதற்கு முன்பே தோன்றிப் பாண்டவர்கள் ஒப்பந்தத்தை மீறிவிட்டார்கள், இவன் யாராக இருந்தாலும் போரிட்டே ஆக வேண்டும் என்று துரியோதனன் பீஷ்மர், த்ரோணர், க்ருபரிடம் சொல்கிறான். பசுக்களை முன்னே அனுப்பிப் படையை அணிவகுக்க ஆணையிடுகிறான்.
summary.ml: പതിമൂന്നു വർഷം പൂർത്തിയാകുംമുമ്പ് പാണ്ഡവർ പ്രത്യക്ഷരായി കരാർ ലംഘിച്ചിരിക്കുന്നുവെന്ന് ദുര്യോധനൻ ഭീഷ്മർ, ദ്രോണർ, കൃപർ എന്നിവരോട് പറയുന്നു. ആരായാലും പോരാടണമെന്ന് അദ്ദേഹം കൽപ്പിക്കുന്നു. പശുക്കളെ മുന്നിലേക്ക് അയക്കാനും, യുദ്ധത്തിന് സേനയെ അണിനിരത്താനും അദ്ദേഹം ഉത്തരവിടുന്നു.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI, Pune) 4.42; e-text by M. Tokunaga and J. D. Smith, © BORI 1999, version of Thu Dec  1 2011

verses.text: वैशंपायन उवाच

meaning.en: Vaishampayana said:

verses.text:
अथ दुर्योधनो राजा समरे भीष्ममब्रवीत् ।
द्रोणं च रथशार्दूलं कृपं च सुमहारथम् ॥

meaning.en: Then King Duryodhana, on the battlefield, spoke to Bhishma, to Drona, a tiger among charioteers, and to Kripa, a great charioteer.

verses.text:
उक्तोऽयमर्थ आचार्यो मया कर्णेन चासकृत् ।
पुनरेव च वक्ष्यामि न हि तृप्यामि तं ब्रुवन् ॥

meaning.en: "Karna and I have said this to the teacher often, and I will say it again, for I never tire of saying it.

verses.text:
पराजितैर्हि वस्तव्यं तैश्च द्वादश वत्सरान् ।
वने जनपदेऽज्ञातैरेष एव पणो हि नः ॥

meaning.en: The defeated ones must live twelve years in the forest and, unrecognized, in the country; this was our wager.

verses.text:
तेषां न तावन्निर्वृत्तं वर्तते तु त्रयोदशम् ।
अज्ञातवासं बीभत्सुरथास्माभिः समागतः ॥

meaning.en: Their thirteenth year is not yet complete, yet Bibhatsu has come before us in the year of hiding.

verses.text:
अनिवृत्ते तु निर्वासे यदि बीभत्सुरागतः ।
पुनर्द्वादश वर्षाणि वने वत्स्यन्ति पाण्डवाः ॥

meaning.en: If Bibhatsu has appeared before the exile is complete, the Pandavas must live another twelve years in the forest.

verses.text:
लोभाद्वा ते न जानीयुरस्मान्वा मोह आविशत् ।
हीनातिरिक्तमेतेषां भीष्मो वेदितुमर्हति ॥

meaning.en: Either greed makes them unaware, or confusion has seized us; Bhishma is the one to judge whether the time is short or over.

verses.text:
अर्थानां तु पुनर्द्वैधे नित्यं भवति संशयः ।
अन्यथा चिन्तितो ह्यर्थः पुनर्भवति चान्यथा ॥

meaning.en: When reckonings differ, doubt always arises, and a matter thought of one way again turns out another.

verses.text:
उत्तरं मार्गमाणानां मत्स्यसेनां युयुत्सताम् ।
यदि बीभत्सुरायातस्तेषां कः स्यात्पराङ्मुखः ॥

meaning.en: Of those who seek the north in order to fight the Matsya army, if Bibhatsu has come, who would turn back?

verses.text:
त्रिगर्तानां वयं हेतोर्मत्स्यान्योद्धुमिहागताः ।
मत्स्यानां विप्रकारांस्ते बहूनस्मानकीर्तयन् ॥

meaning.en: We came here to fight the Matsyas for the Trigartas, who told us of the many wrongs the Matsyas did them.

verses.text:
तेषां भयाभिपन्नानां तदस्माभिः प्रतिश्रुतम् ।
प्रथमं तैर्ग्रहीतव्यं मत्स्यानां गोधनं महत् ॥

meaning.en: We promised them, since they were gripped by fear, that they should first seize the great herds of the Matsyas.

verses.text:
सप्तमीमपराह्णे वै तथा नस्तैः समाहितम् ।
अष्टम्यां पुनरस्माभिरादित्यस्योदयं प्रति ॥

meaning.en: They arranged to do it in the afternoon of the seventh day, and we are to do it on the eighth, toward sunrise.

verses.text:
ते वा गावो न पश्यन्ति यदि व स्युः पराजिताः ।
अस्मान्वाप्यतिसंधाय कुर्युर्मत्स्येन संगतम् ॥

meaning.en: Perhaps they do not see the cattle, or they are defeated, or they have tricked us and made peace with Matsya.

verses.text:
अथ वा तानुपायातो मत्स्यो जानपदैः सह ।
सर्वया सेनया सार्धमस्मान्योद्धुमुपागतः ॥

meaning.en: Or Matsya has come with the countrypeople and the whole army to fight us after getting at them.

verses.text:
तेषामेव महावीर्यः कश्चिदेव पुरःसरः ।
अस्माञ्जेतुमिहायातो मत्स्यो वापि स्वयं भवेत् ॥

meaning.en: Or one of their very powerful men has come at the head, or Matsya himself, to defeat us here.

verses.text:
यद्येष राजा मत्स्यानां यदि बीभत्सुरागतः ।
सर्वैर्योद्धव्यमस्माभिरिति नः समयः कृतः ॥

meaning.en: Whether it is the king of Matsya or Bibhatsu who has come, we have agreed that we must all fight.

verses.text:
अथ कस्मात्स्थिता ह्येते रथेषु रथसत्तमाः ।
भीष्मो द्रोणः कृपश्चैव विकर्णो द्रौणिरेव च ॥

meaning.en: Why then do these best of charioteers, Bhishma, Drona, Kripa, Vikarna and Drona's son, just stay in their chariots?

verses.text:
संभ्रान्तमनसः सर्वे काले ह्यस्मिन्महारथाः ।
नान्यत्र युद्धाच्छ्रेयोऽस्ति तथात्मा प्रणिधीयताम् ॥

meaning.en: All the great charioteers are bewildered at this moment. There is nothing better than fighting; steady yourselves.

verses.text:
आच्छिन्ने गोधनेऽस्माकमपि देवेन वज्रिणा ।
यमेन वापि संग्रामे को हास्तिनपुरं व्रजेत् ॥

meaning.en: If our herd is snatched away, even by Indra the thunderbolt-wielder or by Yama in battle, who would go back to Hastinapura?

verses.text:
शरैरभिप्रणुन्नानां भग्नानां गहने वने ।
को हि जीवेत्पदातीनां भवेदश्वेषु संशयः ।
आचार्यं पृष्ठतः कृत्वा तथा नीतिर्विधीयताम् ॥

meaning.en: Scattered by arrows and broken in the deep forest, which foot soldier would survive? Even the horses are in doubt. Putting the teacher behind us, let the policy be so framed.

verses.text:
जानाति हि मतं तेषामतस्त्रासयतीव नः ।
अर्जुनेनास्य संप्रीतिमधिकामुपलक्षये ॥

meaning.en: He knows their mind, and that is why he seems to frighten us; I see he has an excessive affection for Arjuna.

verses.text:
तथा हि दृष्ट्वा बीभत्सुमुपायान्तं प्रशंसति ।
यथा सेना न भज्येत तथा नीतिर्विधीयताम् ॥

meaning.en: Seeing Bibhatsu approach, he praises him. Let a policy be made so that the army is not broken.

verses.text:
अदेशिका महारण्ये ग्रीष्मे शत्रुवशं गता ।
यथा न विभ्रमेत्सेना तथा नीतिर्विधीयताम् ॥

meaning.en: Let a policy be made so that the army, strayed in a great forest in summer and fallen under the enemy's power, does not wander in confusion.

verses.text:
अश्वानां हेषितं श्रुत्वा का प्रशंसा भवेत्परे ।
स्थाने वापि व्रजन्तो वा सदा हेषन्ति वाजिनः ॥

meaning.en: What is there to praise in an enemy in hearing horses neigh? Horses always neigh, standing or going.

verses.text:
सदा च वायवो वान्ति नित्यं वर्षति वासवः ।
स्तनयित्नोश्च निर्घोषः श्रूयते बहुशस्तथा ॥

meaning.en: Winds always blow, Indra always rains, and thunder is often heard.

verses.text:
किमत्र कार्यं पार्थस्य कथं वा स प्रशस्यते ।
अन्यत्र कामाद्द्वेषाद्वा रोषाद्वास्मासु केवलात् ॥

meaning.en: What has Partha to do with this, or why is he praised, except from desire, hatred or sheer anger against us?

verses.text:
आचार्या वै कारुणिकाः प्राज्ञाश्चापायदर्शिनः ।
नैते महाभये प्राप्ते संप्रष्टव्याः कथंचन ॥

meaning.en: Teachers are compassionate, wise and see the dangers; in a great fear like this they should never be consulted at all.

verses.text:
प्रासादेषु विचित्रेषु गोष्ठीष्वावसथेषु च ।
कथा विचित्राः कुर्वाणाः पण्डितास्तत्र शोभनाः ॥

meaning.en: In ornate palaces, gatherings and houses, scholars shine as they tell varied tales.

verses.text:
बहून्याश्चर्यरूपाणि कुर्वन्तो जनसंसदि ।
इष्वस्त्रे चारुसंधाने पण्डितास्तत्र शोभनाः ॥

meaning.en: They shine as they perform many wonders in the assembly of the people, and in the skill of bow and weapons and neat aim.

verses.text:
परेषां विवरज्ञाने मनुष्याचरितेषु च ।
अन्नसंस्कारदोषेषु पण्डितास्तत्र शोभनाः ॥

meaning.en: They shine in finding others' weak points, in the ways of men, and in the faults of cooking food.

verses.text:
पण्डितान्पृष्ठतः कृत्वा परेषां गुणवादिनः ।
विधीयतां तथा नीतिर्यथा वध्येत वै परः ॥

meaning.en: Putting those scholars, who praise the enemies' virtues, behind us, let a policy be made by which the enemy can be killed.

verses.text:
गावश्चैव प्रतिष्ठन्तां सेनां व्यूहन्तु माचिरम् ।
आरक्षाश्च विधीयन्तां यत्र योत्स्यामहे परान् ॥

meaning.en: Let the cattle be sent on their way and let the army be drawn up at once; and let guards be set where we will fight the enemy."
